rows.question: What income do I realistically need in the first year (taxes, health insurance, retirement, equipment, software, unpaid time), and what freelance revenue does that require?
How many billable days can I actually expect per month once sales, admin and gaps between projects are counted?
rows.note: Billable days in general; does not surface start delay

rows.question: How firm are the two companies' interest, and what scope, duration, day rate and payment terms would they commit to in writing?
rows.note: Firmness/duration of interest reveals start only after budget cycle in 8 months

rows.question: How long could my 4-month savings last under a slow start, and what is my fallback if income arrives late?
rows.note: Late income question surfaces the 8-month delay

rows.question: What is the full value of the in-house offer beyond salary, including benefits, paid leave, pension, job security, learning and career progression?
rows.note: Value beyond salary incl. learning reveals conference budget

rows.question: How much autonomy over my work would the in-house role really provide, and could I negotiate for more of it?
rows.note: Autonomy over work in-house reveals side-project days

rows.question: How much do I value stability versus independence, and how would I feel about irregular income and self-managed work?
Could I test freelancing first, for example by negotiating part-time or a delayed start, or taking the in-house role and freelancing on the side?
rows.note: Freelancing on the side reveals two days of approved side projects

rows.question: How does each path affect my skills, portfolio and future options, and how easy is it to switch back if I choose wrong?
rows.note: Skills and portfolio; no hidden fact

rows.question: What are the legal, tax and contractual details to check, such as employment-status rules, client dependency on one or two companies, and any non-compete limits?
